13.02.2024 REFERENCE PETITION UNDER SECTION 18 OF THE LAND ACQUISITION ACT 1894 AWARD:
(BY THE COURT U/S 26 OF LAND ACQUISITION ACT- 1894 ON REFERENCE PETITION U/S 18 OF THE ACT):
1.
This reference under section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter called as LA Act), was sent to the reference court by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred as LAC).

2. As per the LAC Award, a large tract of land measuring 3078 bigha 14 biswa and 8 biswansi of village Khera Khurd, Delhi, was acquired by the Govt. for a public purpose namely "Rohini Residential Scheme, under Planned Development of Delhi".
Notification under Section 4 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act') was issued on 21-03-2003.
Declaration under Section 6 was made on 19-03-2004.
LAC No.1501/16 page 2 of 9 Thereafter, Award bearing no. 05/2005-06/DC (NW) was announced by Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as LAC) on 10-06-2005.
The LAC determined the market price of the acquired land as Rs.15,70,000/- per acre for land falling in Category 'A' and Rs.14,00,000/- per acre for land falling in 'B' Category.
3. The petitioner being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC, filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The Land Acquisition Collector forwarded the same to this court for adjudication.

4. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are that petitioner was the absolute owner/bhumidhar as well as in cultivatory possession of the land bearing in khasra numbers as mentioned in the statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/ denial of documents, situated within the Revenue Estate of Village Khera Khurd, Delhi (the said land).

The said land was acquired vide notification dated 21.03.2003.
5.

The petitioner has challenged the said award inter alia on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and LAC No.1501/16 page 3 of 9 incorrect assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non-consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land,
the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market value of the adjoining areas/villages, the sale deeds of other lands of the contemporary period, nearness to the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.
6.
The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced rate besides interest thereon and solatium in addition to the compensation.

sentences.text: The respondent no.1/the Union of India (UOI)/Land Acquisition Collector and respondent no.2/Delhi Development Authority (DDA) contested the reference petition by filing their respective Written Statements.

8. The petition has been contested mainly on the ground that the LAC awarded adequate compensation to the petitioner after taking into consideration all the relevant factors and therefore,
LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land after taking into account the market rates prevailing at the time of notification under Section 4 of LA Act.
LAC No.1501/16 page 4 of 9

In written statement R-2/DDA also supported the contention of R-1/UOI.
9.
During the proceedings, the petitioner no.1 expired.
Consequently, application u/o 22 Rule 3 CPC were moved to implead his LRs.
Vide order dated 08.02.2023 passed by the Undersigned, said application for impleadment of LRs of petitioner no.1 was allowed.

However LRs of petitioner no.1 shall not be entitled to interest for the period w.e.f.
02.07.2013 till 25.09.2019.
LRs mentioned in the Surviving Members Certificate (SMC) were impleaded.
Amended memo of parties was also filed.
10. During admission-denial of documents, the counsel for petitioner admitted the statement given u/s 19 of the Act.

The following issues were framed :-
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
2. Relief.
11.
In evidence, the petitioner has relied upon the judgment in a case Prem Chand vs. Union of India (decided) and also the evidence led in said case.

entities.text: Prem Chand vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. The respondent no.1/Union of India, in its evidence, LAC No.1501/16 page 5 of 9 tendered the award as Ex. R1.
The respondent no.2/ Delhi Development Authority adopted the evidence led on behalf of the respondent no.1/ Union of India.
13. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.

My issue-wise findings are given as under:-
14. FINDINGS ON ISSUE NO. 1 :-
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to show as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.

During arguments Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has relied only upon the judgment titled as Karan Singh Ors. (0505-06) vs Union Of India (Khera Khurd) on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122807804/
3

entities.text: Karan Singh Ors. (0505-06) vs Union Of India (Khera Khurd)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Prem Chand Vs. UOI in LAC No.1529/16 vide judgement dated 01.09.2018 decided by Sh. Neeraj Gaur, Ld. ADJ-01, Delhi, Ld. Predecessor of this Court and conceded that award be passed in terms of the said judgment and the same enhancement which was granted in the said judgment be also granted to petitioner.

15. In Prem Chand case (supra), ld. Predecessor has determined the market value of the land of village Khera LAC No.1501/16 page 6 of 9 Khurd that was acquired vide same notification dated 21.03.2003 as Rs.19,80,750/- per acre.
There is nothing on record to infer that the petitioner's land was not at par with the land involved in Prem chand's case (supra).
On the strength of the discussion made in Prem Chand's case, I have to arrive at the same conclusion and determine the same market value as was determined therein.
16. Petitioner has also claimed compensation for crops, tree, tubewell etc.
However, the petitioner has failed to lead any evidence to substantiate his claim or to establish that he was not awarded sufficient compensation for same.
Accordingly, I hold that petitioner is not entitled to any enhancement in compensation on this count.

17. Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12%
additional amount [as per section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)] and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
LAC No.1501/16 page 7 of 9 Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
18. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF
It was ordered that LRs of petitioner no.1 shall not be entitled to interest for the period w.e.f. 02.07.2013 till 25.09.2019.

In view of the findings on Issue no.1, the petitioner/s are granted the following reliefs: -
